h1: Landscaping and property clearing in Sooke
cardSummary: Rural acreage, Sooke Basin waterfront and new subdivisions, where broom, blackberry and wetter weather set the work.
intro: Sooke properties tend to be larger and more rural than in the urban core: acreages in Saseenos and Broomhill, waterfront homes near Whiffin Spit and the Sooke Basin, and newer subdivisions close to the town centre.

Broom, gorse and blackberry can close in a rural lot within a few seasons. Clearing goes further when native trees are kept and invasive material is disposed of following CRD guidance. See [tree and vegetation work](/services/tree-vegetation/) or [request a free quote](/free-quote/?area=sooke).
localRulesIntro: This page does not yet summarise a District of Sooke tree rule, because none has been checked against an official source. Ask the District before removing trees; the regional rules below apply where noted.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply (confirm your property's water supply): lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Broom, gorse and blackberry
conditions.body: Sunny rural edges, fence lines and cleared lots fill quickly with Scotch broom and blackberry, and gorse is on the CRD priority list. Cutting before broom sets seed slows the spread.

conditions.title: Wetter, windier weather
conditions.body: Sooke usually sees more rain and wind than the Victoria core. Drainage, mulch and wind-firm planting matter more here, and lawns can stay soft well into spring.

conditions.title: Check your water supply
conditions.body: The CRD lawn days apply only to properties on the regional supply. Rural lots may be on a private system, so confirm which you are on before planning irrigation.

conditions.title: Waterfront lots on the basin
conditions.body: Homes near Whiffin Spit and the Sooke Basin face salt air and winter storms, which can burn tender planting.

topServices.why: Brush, broom and blackberry clearing is the usual first job on a rural Sooke lot.
Once a lot is cleared, rough mowing and regular visits keep regrowth from taking it back.

jobNotes.title: Fence line held clear over a summer
jobNotes.body: Blackberry was cut out along a fence line, then rough-mown twice through the summer to stop regrowth from the roots.

jobNotes.title: Salt-tolerant replant after storms
jobNotes.body: A waterfront bed scorched by winter storms was replanted with salt- and wind-tolerant shrubs and heavily mulched.
